business_ops.seasonality: Disclosed as material. The RHP carries a dedicated risk factor (Internal Risk Factor 11): 'Our income and sales are subject to seasonal fluctuations and lower income in a peak season may have a disproportionate effect on our results of operations.' The Company states that its sales in certain regions have historically exhibited seasonal fluctuations, reflecting higher sales volumes during festival periods, the wedding season and the harvest season, and that seasonal fluctuations also affect inventory management - a large inventory build-up ahead of peak periods can leave excess stock if sales disappoint, while insufficient inventory in peak seasons can mean missed sales and strained customer relationships. It notes that quarter-on-quarter results may therefore not be comparable or a meaningful indicator, and that it has not so far faced such a demand slowdown or a failure to anticipate seasonal fluctuations. Hedging tenure choices explicitly take seasonal demand patterns (wedding and festive seasons) into account. The underlying demand-cycle description (weddings, festivals, birth occasions, anniversaries and the harvest season creating year-round demand) is attributed in the RHP to the commissioned CRISIL Report; the Company adopts it and states it has aligned its operations accordingly and treats the event-driven demand as a strategic advantage.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light, outsourced manufacturing model with a stated intent to backward-integrate into in-house production. Inbound: the Company maintains a procurement network for gold and silver from RBI-registered bullion banks, independent bullion dealers, imports through the India International Bullion Exchange and exchange of metal from customers; gemstones (rubies, pearls, flat diamonds, emeralds) are procured from Jaipur, Surat, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Thailand. Gold bullion is 86.04% of total purchases in Fiscal 2026 (94.65% in Fiscal 2025, 94.92% in Fiscal 2024). Design is in-house: 15 designers as of July 31, 2026, supported by market research and trend analysis; the Company added 6 SKUs and 1 product category in Fiscal 2026 (9 SKUs / 2 categories in Fiscal 2025, 3 SKUs / 1 category in Fiscal 2024). Manufacturing is entirely outsourced: raw material is supplied to a network of 41 karigars (formal agreements with 29; 25 associated more than 5 years), primarily in Telangana and Maharashtra, who craft, polish and finish ornaments and return them against making charges - the RHP notes this avoids significant capital investment while providing flexibility and scalability. Job work is the mirror arrangement: customers supply raw material, the Company processes it for a fee without taking ownership. Downstream: finished pieces go to government-registered, BIS-approved hallmarking centres for purity certification, then through an in-house quality-control team checking purity, structural integrity, design accuracy, stone quality, stone setting, design symmetry and finishing, then billing, packing and dispatch via in-house delivery executives or third-party logistics for inter-city delivery. Orders arrive by e-mail, the Company's third-party mobile application 'Deepa Jewellers Limited' (commissioned June 25, 2021; 312 / 152 / 110 users in Fiscal 2026 / 2025 / 2024, B2B use only, design-selection interface only) and social media; sales are either from ready-stock inventory or order-based from the design bank. Forward integration into retail is absent - the Company owns no standalone stores and does not sell to end consumers. The planned backward integration is the 6,696 sq ft Proposed Facility in Hyderabad (real wax 3D printer ProJet MJP 300W, vacuum pressure casting machine, induction melting furnace), expected operational before the end of the first half of Fiscal 2027, intended to reduce karigar dependence, lower making charges, improve quality control, limit pilferage and protect design confidentiality; it had not commenced commercial operations as on the date of the RHP. Working capital is short-cycle: inventory holding 18 / 21 / 22 days, debtors 36 / 29 / 32 days, creditors 1 / 1 / 1 day, net operating cycle 53 / 49 / 53 days for Fiscal 2026 / 2025 / 2024. Gold price exposure is managed through hedging instruments of varying tenures.

overview.business_model: The Company sells to businesses, not end consumers. In-house designers create products tailored to customer requirements, market trends and regional preferences; manufacturing is fully outsourced to a network of 41 karigars to whom the Company supplies gold, alloys and precious stones and who return finished ornaments against making charges. Finished jewellery is hallmarked at government-registered, BIS-approved hallmarking centres and supplied to 47 jewellery retail chains and 326 standalone stores (373 customers across 13 states and 1 union territory as of July 31, 2026). Revenue also comes from job work (customer supplies the raw material, the Company processes and returns it for a fee without taking ownership) and from trading of silver ornaments, 18 and 20 karat gold ornaments, precious stones and gold bullion. Revenue from operations was Rs 19,266.76 million in Fiscal 2026, of which vaddanam contributed Rs 8,062.41 million (41.85%) and CNC machine cut bangles Rs 5,948.53 million (30.87%). The Company owns no standalone stores and, as of the RHP date, no manufacturing facility of its own; a first in-house facility in Hyderabad is being set up.

internal_operational.detail: Revenue is concentrated among a few key customers and the Company does not enter into long-term contracts with any of them. Any decision by these customers to reduce or terminate business, or a failure to place orders at past levels, could materially affect business, results of operations and financial condition. Names are withheld as commercially sensitive; none of the top customers are related parties or promoter-linked entities.

internal_operational.detail: A significant portion of revenue comes from two product lines. Any cancellation of purchase orders for these products, or a shift in consumer preference away from them, could adversely affect business, cash flows, financial condition and results of operations.

strategy_growth.detail: The Company competes with organised and unorganised players; some competitors are larger in sales volume, distribution network and brand recall and have greater capital, technical capability and financial resources, and may offer promotional incentives particularly during festivals. Gold jewellery pricing is extremely competitive because of its objectively verifiable value, limiting pricing control. Unorganised competitors operating as partnerships or proprietary concerns are not subject to the Companies Act and may have more structural flexibility.
strategy_growth.evidence: Per the CRISIL Report, the Indian jewellery industry has traditionally been dominated by family-owned businesses which still account for the majority of the industry, while the organised segment has grown rapidly and gained substantial market share.
strategy_growth.title: Significant competition in a highly fragmented Indian jewellery market

strategy_growth.detail: Continued growth depends on cost-effective conversion of existing customers into repeat buyers and attraction of new customers through targeted marketing and brand engagement, which may affect profitability. Customer numbers may decline due to dissatisfaction with product quality, design or pricing, reduced appeal versus competitors, intense competition, or reputational risk and negative publicity.
strategy_growth.evidence: As of July 31, 2026 there were 373 customers, of which 18 have been associated since inception. Duration of association: 2-4 years, 168 customers; 5-7 years, 86 customers; above 7 years, 36 customers.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on converting existing customers into repeat buyers and acquiring new customers

strategy_growth.detail: 100.00% of gold jewellery is currently manufactured through the outsourced karigar model, and the Company intends to scale capacity by establishing an in-house Proposed Facility. Construction, installation and commissioning are subject to regulatory approvals, timely machinery availability, installation challenges, construction and logistical delay and labour constraints. Transitioning from outsourced to in-house manufacturing involves operational, managerial and financial risk including sourcing and retaining skilled manpower, achieving production efficiency and maintaining quality standards.
strategy_growth.evidence: Proposed Facility spanning 6,696.00 square feet in Hyderabad; orders placed for required equipment; operations expected to commence prior to the conclusion of the first half of Fiscal 2027, with no assurance the timeline will be met.
strategy_growth.title: Setting up the Proposed Facility exposes the Company to implementation delay and cost overrun

concerns_observed: Receivables have become the balance sheet: trade receivables of Rs 252.36 crore at March 31, 2026 exceed net worth of Rs 238.07 crore and are up from Rs 131.73 crore a year earlier (13.10% of revenue against 9.43%), against cash of Rs 0.10 crore; layered on top is an unquantified recourse exposure under the electronic vendor financing scheme, where the bank pays the Company on the customer's behalf but can recover from the Company if the customer defaults.

Extreme asymmetry between customer credit and supplier credit: customers get 25-45 day terms (debtor days 36) while suppliers allow one day (creditor days 1, trade payables Rs 0.09 crore), so essentially the entire working-capital cycle is funded by borrowing - Rs 127.41 crore outstanding at July 31, 2026, all of the bank portion from a single lender, Yes Bank, against a Rs 115 crore sanction.

The entire manufacturing base is outside the company: 100.00% of gold jewellery is made by 41 non-exclusive karigars, formal agreements exist with only 29, the number engaged has fallen to 29 (FY2026) from 34 (FY2024), some karigars sub-delegate work, and the mitigating in-house facility (6,696 sq ft, Rs 2.28 crore spent to March 31, 2026 from internal accruals) has not commenced operations and is not an object of the Offer.

Supplier and sourcing concentration is worse than customer concentration: top 10 suppliers were 91.81% of FY2026 purchases (Supplier 1 alone 24.18%) with no long-term contracts, and 56.73% of FY2026 gold (739.04 kg of 1,302.64 kg) came from 'exchange from customers' rather than a bullion market, with IIBX sourcing nil.

Concentration on two products and one region: vaddanam (41.85%) plus CNC machine-cut bangles (30.87%) were 72.72% of FY2026 revenue and the mix between them swung materially in a single year (vaddanam 34.58% to 41.85%, bangles 41.82% to 30.87%); South India was 94.37% of revenue, Telangana alone 41.58%.

The two most important premises are rented from the Chairman and Managing Director: the Registered Office (4,464 sq ft) and the Proposed Facility (6,696 sq ft) are both leased from Ashish Agarwal for 9 years 11 months from November 28, 2025, related-party rent jumped to Rs 48.4 lakhs in FY2026 from Rs 1.2 lakhs in FY2025, and Ashish Agarwal has additionally mortgaged the Registered Office premises to Yes Bank.

The governance layer was assembled immediately before the filing: all three Independent Directors were appointed September 1, 2025, the CFO on October 17, 2025 and the Company Secretary on November 28, 2025; only one Director (Sirisha Chintapalli) has prior listed-company board experience; and the Risk Management Committee that oversees gold hedging is chaired by Dev Agarwal, aged 23, with over five years of industry experience and a Rs 90 lakh per annum basic salary.

A long list of RoC filing failures spanning nine years: Form CHG-1 for FY2017, FY2018, FY2019 and FY2022; both ADT-1s and the ADT-3; DIR-12s; MGT-14s including the one for the November 28, 2025 bonus allotment; DPT-3 for FY2019 and FY2025; AOC-4 XBRL for FY2022; and BEN-2 for Ashish Agarwal's beneficial-ownership declaration - all filed late with penalty fees.

Degree certificates could not be traced from the issuing universities for five people including Ashish Agarwal, the Promoter, Chairman and Managing Director, and Company Secretary Vandana Modani; the RHP relies on provisional documents and university correspondence.

Brand and IP are unprotected: all four trademark applications (two logos and the taglines filed July 19, 2025 and December 3, 2025) were still pending at July 31, 2026, no jewellery designs are registered under the Designs Act, 2000, no patents exist, and advertising spend was Rs 6.14 million or 0.03% of total expenses in FY2026.
data_gaps: No valuation can be formed: the Price Band, Floor Price, Cap Price, Offer Price, Fresh Issue share count, total Offer size, post-Offer paid-up capital, market capitalisation, P/E and P/B for the issuer are all printed as '[.]' in this RHP. The peer table prints Highest 57.56 / Lowest 10.08 / Average 23.92 P/E and no median.

Post-Offer promoter and promoter-group holding is '[.]', dilution percentage is undeterminable, and the entire Capital Structure lock-in table (shares locked in, until-dates, acquisition prices, pre/post-Offer percentages) is printed as '[.]' and marked to be completed before filing the Prospectus with the RoC; anchor lock-in exists as a rule (50% for 90 days, 50% for 30 days) but with no dates.

The General Corporate Purposes amount, its FY2027/FY2028 deployment and both Total rows of the objects utilisation and deployment tables are '[.]', so total project cost is not stated; the OFS share of total Offer size is also '[.]'.

No capacity-utilisation percentage is printed anywhere for the issuer in any year, and no FY2025 karigar capacity figure exists (only 2,155 kg in FY2024 and 2,925 kg in FY2026), so utilisation against the expanded capacity cannot be read from the document.
No top-5 subtotal is printed for either customer or supplier concentration - only top-1 and top-10 - so the middle of both distributions is unobservable.

Facility-level interest rates are not disclosed: only ranges of 8.00%-10.00% (TBILL 3M + 2.72%, MCLR or external-benchmark linked) for fund-based working capital and 2.00%-3.00% decided at disbursement for the gold metal loan.
The B2B customer-type split is given only in amounts (retail chains Rs 1,466.32 crore, standalone stores Rs 460.35 crore in FY2026), with no percentages printed and none derived.

Dev Agarwal's lifetime weighted average cost of acquisition is not printed - he is a Promoter but not a Selling Shareholder, so only the 'Nil' bonus-issue price for his 1,485,000 last-year shares appears; his 99,000 gifted shares of March 23, 2021 carry no stated cost.
Pages 199-206 of the source PDF (part of the 'Our Business' chapter) are scanned images with no extractable text; no absence of fact should be inferred from that range.

The reported FY2026 total current liabilities of Rs 2.70 crore sit oddly against Rs 111.12 crore of total debt and Rs 127.41 crore of borrowings at July 31, 2026; the working-capital table's current-liabilities definition appears to exclude borrowings, but the filing does not reconcile the two presentations.
monitorables: Whether operating cash flow turns positive in FY2027 after two negative years, and whether debtor days hold at 36 as revenue scales - receivables already exceed net worth.

Commissioning of the 6,696 sq ft Proposed Facility by the end of H1 FY2027 as stated; all regulatory and manufacturing approvals for it were still to be applied for as at the RHP date, and equipment (ProJet MJP 300W real-wax 3D printer, vacuum pressure casting machine, induction melting furnace) was only in the installation phase.
Physical volume, not rupee revenue: gold quantity sold against the 2,925 kg per annum karigar capacity, and whether the 1,644 kg FY2026 level recovers past the 1,889 kg FY2025 peak.
Whether the 7.60% FY2026 EBITDA margin survives a flat or falling gold-price year, and whether the inventory hedge ratio (0.53 to 0.76 to 0.84) is maintained and by what instrument.

Karigar network health: 41 in the pool but only 29 formally contracted and only 29 engaged in FY2026 against 34 in FY2024; watch formalisation of the remaining 12 and any migration of work to the in-house facility.

Quality and return metrics as volumes scale: 24 customers rejected or returned 32.47 kg of gold for quality defects in FY2026 (21 customers / 25.72 kg in FY2025), unsold jewellery accepted back was 93.84 kg, and gold lost in manufacturing rose to 5,126.89 grams from 3,654.82 grams.

Deployment against the stated schedule - Rs 125 crore of net proceeds in FY2027 and Rs 90 crore in FY2028 - and CARE Ratings' quarterly monitoring reports, since no bank or agency appraised the objects.

Repayment or continuation of the Rs 44.43 crore of promoter loans at 6% (Ashish Rs 14.03 crore, Seema Rs 17.25 crore, Dev Rs 13.14 crore at July 31, 2026), which are repayable on demand subject to Yes Bank consent and are not an object of the Offer.
Registration outcome of the four pending class-14 trademark applications, and the opening of the intended Bengaluru sales office in FY2027.

Any regulatory action arising from the historical RoC filing delays and from the dissolved Promoter Group firms M/s Deepa Jewellers (dissolved November 27, 2025) and M/s Deepa Gold (December 6, 2025), whose residual tax and compliance exposure is disclosed but unquantified.
open_questions: What actually drove EBITDA margin from 4.01% to 7.60% in one year? The extracted domains carry no mix, pricing, making-charge or inventory-gain explanation, and the two flagship products moved in opposite directions (vaddanam up 34.58% to 41.85%, CNC bangles down 41.82% to 30.87%).

What is the 'internal hedging mechanism' that carried 84.07% of FY2026 inventory? The RHP describes it only as being executed near-simultaneously with customer orders; it is not a contracted instrument, exchange forwards were nil in all three years, and its effectiveness is untested in the document.

Why did volume fall to 1,644 kg while capacity was raised to 2,925 kg per annum and 373 customers were served - price-driven order shrinkage, karigar constraint (29 engaged versus 34 in FY2024), or a deliberate mix shift toward job work (387 kg to 757 kg)?
How large is the e-VFS recourse exposure? The Company is liable to the bank if a customer fails to pay, but no outstanding e-VFS amount, customer count or tenor is disclosed anywhere in the filing.
How is 'exchange from customers' gold - 739.04 kg, 56.73% of FY2026 sourcing - priced and settled, and does it interact with the receivable balance or the reported margin?
Was the previous auditor's lack of a valid ICAI peer-review certificate known before the IPO preparation, and does the April 2, 2025 resignation for 'pre-occupancy in other assignments' relate to it?

Is FY2026 RoNW of 56.45% - well above every listed peer in the RHP's own table - a function of superior economics or simply a small equity base (NAV per share Rs 29.03 against peers at Rs 70.29 to Rs 129.14) carrying Rs 111.12 crore of debt?
Will the promoter loans of Rs 44.43 crore be repaid post-listing, and if so from what source, given no part of the Net Proceeds is earmarked for debt repayment?
verdict.our_read: Deepa Jewellers is a Hyderabad B2B gold-jewellery house that designs, hallmarks and distributes but manufactures nothing itself - 100% of output comes from 41 outsourced karigars (formal agreements with only 29) sold to 373 South Indian retailers - and the make-or-break tension is whether the FY2026 step-up (revenue Rs 1,926.68 crore, PAT Rs 104.79 crore, EBITDA margin 7.60% against 4.01% in FY2025) is durable operating improvement or a gold-price windfall, given that gold quantity sold actually fell to 1,644 kg from 1,889 kg and operating cash flow was negative Rs 14.73 crore for a second consecutive year while the Rs 250 crore fresh issue's only quantified use, Rs 215 crore, is to fund exactly that working-capital gap.

parameter_scores.audit_and_disclosure_quality: Mixed - disclosure is unusually granular (karigar counts, gold loss in grams, returned kilograms, hedge ratios) and litigation, contingent liabilities and group companies are affirmatively nil, but the prior auditor lacked a valid ICAI peer-review certificate and FY2024 had to be re-audited.
parameter_scores.balance_sheet_risk: Elevated - receivables of Rs 252.36 crore exceed net worth of Rs 238.07 crore, creditor days of 1 against debtor days of 36, single-lender dependence on Yes Bank (Rs 115 crore sanctioned) plus Rs 44.43 crore of on-demand promoter loans and unquantified e-VFS recourse.
parameter_scores.capital_efficiency: Optically outstanding, structurally leveraged - RoNW 56.45% and RoCE 52.08% in FY2026 on net fixed assets of Rs 2.26 crore, but on a Rs 238.07 crore net worth carrying Rs 111.12 crore of debt and NAV per share of Rs 29.03 against peers at Rs 70.29-129.14.
parameter_scores.cash_conversion: Poor - operating cash flow negative in two of three years (negative Rs 14.73 crore FY2026, negative Rs 9.86 crore FY2025) against PAT of Rs 104.79 crore and Rs 40.58 crore; closing cash Rs 0.10 crore.
parameter_scores.concentration_risk: High on both axes - vaddanam plus CNC bangles at 72.72% of FY2026 revenue and South India at 94.37% (Telangana alone 41.58%).
parameter_scores.customer_dependence: High but not captive - top 10 at 64.67% of FY2026 revenue with no long-term contracts and no order book, though the largest customer is only 16.80% and 373 customers include named national chains.
parameter_scores.governance: Recently constructed and promoter-centred - three Independent Directors, CFO and CS all appointed between September and November 2025, one Director with listed-company experience, registered office and proposed facility both leased from the CMD, and a nine-year record of late RoC filings.
parameter_scores.growth_quality: Weak beneath the headline - revenue Rs 1,024.57 crore to Rs 1,926.68 crore over three years, but FY2026 volume fell to 1,644 kg from 1,889 kg while average gold price rose to Rs 115,996 from Rs 75,842 per 10 grams.
parameter_scores.margin_durability: Unproven - EBITDA margin doubled from 3.49% to 7.60% in two years with no disclosed driver, in a business the RHP calls high-volume, low-margin with limited pricing control.
parameter_scores.operating_control: Thin - 100.00% of manufacturing outsourced to 41 karigars with formal agreements for only 29, hallmarking outsourced, no owned plant, and the in-house facility not yet commissioned.
parameter_scores.promoter_skin_and_exit: Cost base near zero - 61,500,000 of 82,000,000 pre-Offer shares from the November 28, 2025 3:1 bonus, Nil securities premium, and a certified weighted average cost of acquisition of Rs 0.50 per share for both Selling Shareholders offering up to 11,848,340 shares; offsetting this, no promoter shares are pledged.
parameter_scores.supplier_dependence: Very high - top 10 suppliers at 91.81% of FY2026 purchases, Supplier 1 at 24.18%, no long-term contracts, and 56.73% of gold sourced as exchange from customers.
parameter_scores.use_of_proceeds: Working-capital funding, not capacity - Rs 215 crore of the Rs 250 crore fresh issue goes to inventory and receivables (Rs 125 crore FY2027, Rs 90 crore FY2028), nothing to capex, no external appraisal, but CARE Ratings appointed as monitoring agency.
parameter_scores.valuation: Not assessable - the Price Band, Offer Price, offer size, market capitalisation, P/E and P/B are all printed as '[.]' in this RHP, so no expensive-or-cheap judgement can be formed from the document.

red_flags: Profit is not turning into cash, and the IPO is being raised to plug that gap: FY2026 PAT of Rs 104.79 crore came with operating cash flow of negative Rs 14.73 crore, the second negative year running after negative Rs 9.86 crore in FY2025, driven by a Rs 120.63 crore increase in trade receivables and a Rs 4.58 crore inventory build; taxes paid of Rs 38.48 crore exceeded the Rs 23.75 crore of cash generated from operations before tax; and the sole quantified object of the Rs 250 crore fresh issue is Rs 215 crore of long-term working capital for exactly that inventory and receivable build.

FY2026 revenue growth is price-led, not volume-led: revenue rose from Rs 1,397.01 crore to Rs 1,926.68 crore while the quantity of gold jewellery sold FELL to 1,644 kg from 1,889 kg (FY2024: 1,739 kg), against a CRISIL period-average gold price that moved from Rs 60,624 to Rs 75,842 to Rs 115,996 per 10 grams over the same three years - and physical volume is below the FY2024 level even though karigar capacity was expanded to 2,925 kg per annum.

The margin step-up is unexplained in the filing: EBITDA margin went 3.49% (FY2024) to 4.01% (FY2025) to 7.60% (FY2026) and PAT margin 2.37% to 2.90% to 5.44%, in a business the RHP itself describes as a high-volume, low-margin environment with limited pricing control because gold's value is objectively verifiable; no driver for the near-doubling is disclosed in the extracted domains, and it coincides with the sharpest gold-price year of the three.

The three-year audited track record rests on a re-audit forced by an auditor defect: the previous statutory auditor Prahalad Khandelwal & Co did not hold a valid ICAI peer-review certificate, so FY2024 financial information had to be re-audited by NSVR & Associates LLP as special-purpose Ind AS statements (report dated November 28, 2025); Prahalad Khandelwal & Co had resigned on April 2, 2025 citing pre-occupancy in other assignments, and NSVR was appointed on May 30, 2025 into the casual vacancy.

Gold-price hedging in the two most recent years ran entirely on an undefined in-house mechanism: FY2026 inventory of Rs 82.94 crore was hedged to the extent of Rs 69.73 crore (ratio 0.84) and FY2025 Rs 59.44 crore (0.76) 'solely through the internal hedging mechanism', with forward contracts on commodity exchanges nil in all three years and the gold metal loan - the only instrument-backed hedge, covering 52.37% in FY2024 - no longer counted as a hedge, even though a Rs 100 crore gold metal loan sublimit was sanctioned and Rs 12.56 crore was outstanding at July 31, 2026.

Pre-Offer capital is overwhelmingly bonus stock issued inside the disclosure window while the sellers exit at near-zero cost: 61,500,000 of the 82,000,000 pre-Offer shares came from the 3:1 bonus of November 28, 2025 (within 18 months of the August 25, 2026 RHP), the securities premium account is Nil because all cash capital was subscribed at Rs 10 face value in 2016, and Ashish Agarwal and Seema Agarwal are together selling up to 11,848,340 shares at a certified weighted average cost of acquisition of Rs 0.50 per Rs 2 share.
strengths_observed: Profit scaled faster than revenue across the three restated years: PAT Rs 24.35 crore (FY2024) to Rs 40.58 crore (FY2025) to Rs 104.79 crore (FY2026); EBITDA Rs 35.77 crore to Rs 56.01 crore to Rs 146.34 crore; EPS Rs 2.97 to Rs 4.95 to Rs 12.78. FY2026 RoNW of 56.45% is above every company in the RHP's own peer table (Shanti Gold 37.34%, Khazanchi 32.45%, Shringar 26.29%, Sky Gold 23.88%, RBZ 20.11%).

Affirmatively clean legal and off-balance-sheet position: nil outstanding criminal, regulatory and material civil litigation for the Company, Promoters and Directors alike; tax proceedings nil in both count and demand amount for all three parties; no contingent liabilities under Ind AS 37 at March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024; no Group Companies; no promoter shares pledged or encumbered; total outstanding dues to 12 creditors of only Rs 0.90 million.

Real, named and broad B2B customer franchise rather than a captive one: 373 customers (47 retail chains, 326 standalone stores) across 13 states and 1 UT as of July 31, 2026, including Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, Lalithaa Jewellery Mart, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri, Bhima Jewels and Manoj Vaibhav; 18 associated since inception and 36 for over seven years; the largest single customer is 16.80% of FY2026 revenue and the RHP states none of the top customers is a related or promoter-linked party.

Genuinely asset-light with a short cash cycle: net fixed assets of Rs 2.26 crore and CWIP of Rs 2.21 crore support Rs 1,926.68 crore of FY2026 revenue; net operating cycle 53 days (inventory 18 days, debtors 36 days) and inventory turnover of 20.91x in FY2026 against 17.16x in FY2024.

External financial validation exists despite no appraisal of the objects: CRISIL Ratings assigned CRISIL A-/Stable on Rs 115 crore of bank facilities (dated March 30, 2026) with no downgrade in FY2024-FY2026, and CARE Ratings Limited was appointed monitoring agency under an agreement dated August 4, 2026 with quarterly reporting.

Outsourced capacity and design throughput both expanded: karigar processing capacity from 2,155 kg per annum (FY2024) to 2,925 kg per annum (FY2026); job-work volume processed from 387 kg to 757 kg; SKUs from 61 to 76 and product categories from 11 to 14; the Vijayawada sales office opened November 2025 helped lift non-South revenue from 0.45% to 5.63% (Maharashtra alone 0.39% to 5.57%).
